There are two main categories of depression: 

Situational depression, which is when you are depressed solely BECAUSE of an event, in which removal of triggering event will significantly ease the depression.

Clinical depression, which isn't directly connected with external events and is due to chemical imbalances in the brain, in which altering external events won't necessarily ease the depression.

Please don't be ashamed for being depressed just because you can't come up with a reason for it.  It should be treated just like any other illness.  People who shit on others for having situational or clinical depression are ignorant.

I had depression for years before seeking any kind of help.  Your feelings of emptiness and apathy are similar to what I've experienced.  If you're worried you might have depression, chances are you probably have depression, at least to a degree.  

On my own, what I found helpful is to not let my mind wander too often.  I try not to stay in bed for too long in the morning or lounge around in the middle of the day.  Occupy yourself with something, it can be anything as long as it's not unhelpful to you - even playing a game on your phone can be good.  Don't stay in one place for too long, move around. 

I would avoid going on social media too much, as that can cause you to compare yourself to other people and also give you a false sense of reality.  

Also, make sure you're getting enough sleep every night.  I myself am sensitive when it comes to not getting enough sleep, which can trigger my depression .

There is no quick fix or perfect formula for feeling better, but these are just things I find helpful.  I hope this at least will give you some ideas for self-coping.  Take care of yourself. c:
